title: What is known about 1RB0RC_1LC0RD_0LD0LC_1RE0LA_0RA1RF_1RE---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RC_1LC0RD_0LD0LC_1RE0LA_0RA1RF_1RE---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

It is one of five machines that share states A to E (1RB0RC_1LC0RD_0LD0LC_1RE0LA_0RA?RF_F---) and differ only in what E writes on a 1 and in state F. All five run the same machinery, a nested base-5 odometer built from blocks of the word 1000; they differ only in how a rare collision is resolved, the one place where state F is used.
verdict: The question is open. The run is understood as a nested odometer whose regular rounds are proved in Lean, but its irregular events (blocks running empty) are only observed, not proved to come from a closed list; nothing like a proof of non-halting is in sight.

Where a halt would have to come from. The machine halts only in F reading a 1, and F is entered only from E reading a 1, right after D wrote a 1 on a 0: so a halt needs D>0 1 1 somewhere. In the run F is entered only twice in the first 2·109 steps (steps 49,249 and 390,893,438), always when two g4 gadgets meet across an empty block (or at a gadget made by such an event), and it always reads a 0.

No closed set of shapes. The irregular gadgets form a closed alphabet, but the tape language they span contains halting tapes: the trap 101, and a tape of regular gadgets with every block of length ≥ 2 that halts (both proved in Lean). So the decision has to come from relations between block lengths, which no shape-level (CTL-style) argument captures.
Pushed to 1.91·1017 steps. An accelerated simulator, validated round by round against the plain machine up to 2·1010 steps, finds no halt and no trap in the first 1.91·1017 steps.
Family F05. One of 40 holdouts on the same five-state core; the family's exact block-list map runs this machine for 1.9·10200 steps without a halt.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: One of 40 holdouts on the same five-state core
claims.text: In frame A all 40 machines have states A to E of 1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE?LF_1LA0LB_??--- and differ in D1 (0LF or 1LF), in F0 and in the start state. This machine is the mirror image of that table with the states renamed A→B, B→C, C→D, D→E, E→A, F→F, with D1 = 1LF and F0 = 1LD: step_img proves that every step of the machine is a step of 1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE1LF_1LA0LB_1LD---, and halts_iff that it halts from blank tape if and only if 1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE1LF_1LA0LB_1LD--- halts from blank tape started in state E. The tables of all 40 are compared by frames.py.

claims.title: The family's visit rule and its closed form
claims.text: In frame A a visit starts with the head in state A on the 0 in front of plain blocks (10)^b1 1 (10)^b2 1 … 1 and ends when the head first steps left of that cell. go_spec proves for every depth that a clean visit turns the list l into go n l in exactly goT n l steps (the first block is spread, the rest gets five visits, the first block is folded back 5 shorter); go_closed gives the closed form (b1−5, b2−18, b3−90, …, bk+12·5k−2) when b1 is odd and at least 7, the other blocks even and block i at least 2+18·5i−2. visit states it as a run of this machine. Also proved: the birth of a block, and that the entry into F after a visit that ends in state C on a phase-1 tail reads a 0 (fevent, fevent_reads_zero). The proofs are generated for this machine's own frame-A table; they never use F0.

claims.title: What a clean visit conserves
claims.text: For the blocks after the first, the last one left out: a clean visit (a list the closed form applies to) changes neither the residue of block i modulo 18·5<sup>i−2</sup> nor the drift b<sub>i+1</sub> − 5·b<sub>i</sub> of two neighbours. So these numbers change only at the exceptional events (a block running out, a birth, an entry into F, the left end). This is a law between events, not a proof that the machine never halts.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.9·10<sup>200</sup> steps (exact block-list map)
claims.text: The machine run as a map on block lists (clean visits by the closed form, a Lean theorem; every other visit by the exact run-length simulator, memoised) reaches step 1.9·10200 without a halt: 503 returns to the left end, 211 entries into F, all reading 0, all with the tape of the proved harmless kind around the head (010001000100[F]011010101010 (182×); 010001000100[F]011010110101 (29×)). The list has 143 blocks at the last left-end event. Its F-events (step and cell read) agree with the plain cell-by-cell simulation of the machine on the first 3·109 steps (2 F-events).

claims.title: Halting would need two exceptional events close together
claims.text: A clean visit cannot halt, and in the runs every exceptional event with long blocks around it ends without a halt; short lists of the same shape do halt. When block i runs out, the next block has about the length of their drift, so a second event close by needs a drift near 0 at that moment. Observed at the left-end events of this run: after step 10<sup>20</sup> the smallest drift in absolute value is 28,930, after step 10<sup>100</sup> it is 128,916. New drifts are made of sums and differences of earlier blocks, which grow with the run, so close pairs of events should become ever rarer; but nothing proved keeps a drift away from 0, and the figures are sampled at the left-end events only.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 81,407 cells have been visited and 20,546 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Conversion sweeps
claims.text: Moving right, A, B, D, E turn the words 0100, 1000, 0001, 0010 into 1010 or 0101; moving left, C turns every two 10s into one 1000 (shifted), and turns a separating 1 into a 0. These are what a sweep does to a block: by ↔ a2y with a = 10, b = 1000.

claims.title: Regular odometer rounds
claims.text: With the head in D at the left end, the tape bk G1 by1 G2 … (gadgets g0 = 1001, g1 = 1001100, g2 = 100110, g3 = 10011, g4 = 10010, s = 0) goes to the next such configuration by one round: k gains one b and the first gadget advances: g0→g1 takes a b from the block after it, g1→g2→g3 change nothing else, g4→g0 moves a b from the block after to the block before, s→g0 takes one from the block before, and g3→g4 carries into the next gadget. Proved for every kind of first gadget and every kind of gadget receiving a carry, for all block lengths ≥ 3.

claims.title: Resets
claims.text: When a carry runs through all gadgets (all are g3) to the last one, the head sweeps to the right end and back: every gadget becomes s, every block but the first gains one b, and a new level b g1 appears at the left. Proved for one and two levels.

claims.title: The collision, where F is used
claims.text: bk g4 g4 by g2 … (two g4 with an empty block between): the round enters F once, on a 0, and the pair merges into a g2 and the next gadget advances (g2 → g3); from then on the tape is the same as for …_0RA1RF_0RC---, two steps earlier.

claims.title: The odometer explains the run
claims.text: Sampling the run each time the head is at the left end in D (1.5·109 steps): 35,422 rounds are regular odometer rounds and 35 are not; those are resets and rounds where a block has run empty (merging gadgets into short-lived ones such as 100, 1, 10).

claims.title: F entered rarely, always on a 0
claims.text: F is entered twice in the first 2·109 steps (steps 49,249 and 390,893,438), each time in a collision of two g4 (or a carry into a gadget left by one), reading a 0.

claims.title: The run to 10<sup>10</sup>-10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: At the full sweeps (the head at the right end in A) the tape is ax1 1 ax2 1 …; the last one before 1011 steps is at step 32,109,749,209 (as for the F = 0RC machine, two steps earlier) with blocks 137466 24602 19874 26470 31074 14 133. The first blocks are the same in all five machines (the left levels regrow the same way after every reset); they differ only to the right of the first collision.

claims.title: The trap: 101 halts
claims.text: With the head in D on bk+1 1 0 1 1, whatever follows, the machine halts after 4k+15 steps. The stretch 101 1 is the transient gadget 10 (left by the collision g4 0 g2) meeting the transient gadget 1 (left by another collision) across an empty block.

claims.title: Gadget shapes alone cannot prove non-halting
claims.text: From the head in D on b6 g4 b5 g3 b2 s b2 g0 (b = 1000; only the regular gadgets, every block of length ≥ 2) the machine halts, after 3,275 steps. So the set of tapes "regular gadgets with any block lengths" contains halting configurations, and an invariant that closes must say something about the block lengths, not only about which gadgets occur where. Without s: b6 g4 b2 g4 b2 g4 b2 g0, after 91,992 steps (simulation).

claims.title: The closed-set search over shapes
claims.text: py/shapes.py runs every round symbolically (blocks either empty or of any length ≥ 1, split whenever the run needs it) over prefixes of up to three gadgets. The alphabet of gadgets closes: the regular ones with 1, 10, 100, 1001101, 10011010, 10011011, 100110110, 1001101100, and every irregular gadget seen in 2·1010 steps of the run splits into these. But the search does not close. 35 prefixes halt, all through the trap above. 8,352 of 29,979 prefixes still need a longer prefix: carry chains through g3, and runs of empty blocks the head walks through.

claims.title: Irregular events in 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: 138,748 regular rounds and 47 irregular ones. The transient gadgets 1, 10, 100, … do occur, sometimes next to another gadget across an empty block (g3 0 1, g4 0 10), but never as 10 0 1, the trap.

claims.title: An accelerated simulator, checked round by round
claims.text: py/accsim.py works on the list of (stretch, block length) at each return of the head to the left end. Each round is a symbolic symtm run on a prefix of the list, with the blocks symbolic. It is cached by shape and reused with exact step counts, and recomputed with exact values when a result depends on small blocks. Up to 19,999,759,940 steps it agrees with the plain machine on the tape and the step count of every one of 138,795 rounds.

claims.title: No halt in 1.91·10<sup>17</sup> steps
claims.text: The accelerated run reaches step 190,534,573,657,785,389 (465,979,676 rounds, 40 minutes, one core) without a halt. There it has 13 gadgets and a first block of 102,084,465. On the way, 38 kinds of irregular stretch occur. Two blocks run empty side by side in 3,936 rounds. The atom 10 stands before an empty block in 0 rounds, so the trap 10 0 1 is never formed.

claims.title: Why it is hard
claims.text: The odometer itself is regular, but the block lengths it drains come from earlier resets, and when a block runs empty the gadgets on both sides merge in ways that depend on their phases mod 5. The sequence of these events, and whether one ever produces D>0 1 1, looks irregular; CTL with 4 to 8 states finds no closed invariant.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A proof of non-halting needs an invariant that relates block lengths (for example, that the gadget 10 never meets the gadget 1 across an empty block). Shapes alone do not suffice: witness_halts gives a tape of regular gadgets from which the machine halts.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE1LF_1LA0LB_1LD--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LC_0RC1RF_1RD0RE_1LE0RA_0LA0LE_1RB--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 1 other holdout (listed on the explainer page).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine is a nested counter: the tape is a row of blocks, and between them small gadgets count to five and carry to the right, like the wheels of an odometer that eat the blocks they sit between. This page runs the real machine in your browser and explains the counter; the rounds of the counter are proved in Lean.

facts.text: No halt in the accelerated simulator, checked against the plain machine.
Every regular round of the counter is a theorem.
State F is entered only in rare collisions, always on a 0.

sections.heading: One core, forty machines
html:
This machine is one of 40 holdouts built on the same five states. Written in one common frame (frame A), every one of them has the table

stateABCDEF
reads 01RB0RC1LD0LE1LAF0
reads 10LC0RB0RE0LF or 1LF0LBhalt

and they differ in three things only: the bit that D writes on its way into F (D1), what F does on a 0 (F0), and the state the run starts in. This machine is the mirror image (left and right exchanged) of the core with D1 = 1LF and F0 = 1LD, that is of 1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE1LF_1LA0LB_1LD---, with the states renamed A→B, B→C, C→D, D→E, E→A, F→F (frame G); its start state A is the core's state E. So its run from blank tape is, step for step and mirrored, the run of 1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE1LF_1LA0LB_1LD--- started in state E on blank tape, and the block lists below read right to left on this machine's own tape. Lean proves this for the machine's own table (halts_iff in lean/Family.lean): it halts from blank tape exactly if the frame-A table halts from blank tape in state E.

What the 40 machines share. States A to E never enter F while they run the nested counter, so between two entries into F all 40 machines do the same thing, and one law covers them. In frame A the tape is a list of blocks (10)^b; a visit to the list [b1, …, bk] makes five visits to the list without its first block. When the blocks are large and of the right parity (a clean visit) this has a closed form: b1 loses 5, block i loses 18·5i−2, the last block gains 12·5k−2. Both the recursion and the closed form are Lean theorems for every depth, on each of the 40 tables (go_spec, go_closed). Two quantities are therefore conserved by every clean visit (visit_conserves): the residue of block i modulo 18·5i−2, and the drift bi+1 − 5·bi of two neighbouring blocks (neither the first nor the last). The residue fixes at which phase and with which small value a block will run out; the drift is the length the next block still has at that moment.

This machine's run, seen from the left end. Each time the head comes back to the left end of the tape (frame A) the tape is a plain list of blocks. Move the slider through these moments: the middle blocks drain at their fixed rates, the last block grows, a block that runs out disappears and its neighbours merge, and new blocks are born at the right end. The list is from the exact block-list map (below), which was checked against the plain simulation of the machine on the F-events of the first 3·109 steps.

How far it has been run. The exact block-list map (clean visits by the proved closed form, every other visit by an exact run-length simulation) runs this machine for 1.9·10200 steps without a halt: 503 returns to the left end, 211 entries into F, every one reading 0, with the tape around the head 010001000100[F]011010101010 (182×, F reads 0); 010001000100[F]011010110101 (29×, F reads 0). Every one of these entries is the kind proved harmless in Lean (fevent, fevent_reads_zero): a visit ends in state C on the 0 of a phase-1 tail, and F then reads the last cell of a 1000.

The sixteen variants. The 40 machines are 16 choices of (D1, F0), each from up to three start states. Machines marked with the same run letter had exactly the same block list at their last left-end event (an observation, not a proof); they are still separate halting questions until that is proved.

Why this does not settle halting. A clean visit cannot halt, and an isolated exceptional event (one block running out between long neighbours, a birth, the harmless F-event) does not halt in any run so far. Short block lists of the same shape do halt, so a proof has to control the block lengths: it would have to show that two exceptional events never fall close together, that is, that a drift is never small when its block runs out. The drifts only change at exceptional events, where they are sums and differences of large earlier blocks; nothing is known that keeps them away from 0. Observed in this run, at the left-end events: after step 1020 the smallest drift in absolute value is 28,930, after step 10100 it is 128,916. That is evidence, not a proof, and it is sampled at the left-end events only.

sections.heading: Blocks that change form at every sweep
html: The tape is made of two words, a = 10 and b = 1000. Moving right, the head turns every b it crosses into aa; moving left, it turns aa back into b. So a block is a2y or by depending on which way the head last went through it. The blocks are separated by short gadgets: g0 = 1001, g1 = 1001100, g2 = 100110, g3 = 10011, g4 = 10010, or a bare 0 (s).

sections.heading: An odometer of five-state wheels
html: Look at the tape each time the head comes back to the left end in state D. It reads bk G1 by1 G2 by2 … Gn. One round later the first block has one more b and the first gadget has advanced one step in the cycle g0 → g1 → g2 → g3 → g4 → g0:

step of the wheelalso
g0 → g1the block after it loses one b
g1 → g2, g2 → g3nothing
g3 → g4carry: the next gadget advances
g4 → g0one b moves from the block after to the block before
s → g0the block before loses one b

So gadget i+1 turns once for every five turns of gadget i, exactly like an odometer, and each full turn of a wheel drains two b from the block on its right. Every one of these rounds is a theorem in Lean, for all block lengths.

When a carry runs off the last gadget, the head sweeps across the whole tape and back (a reset): all gadgets become s, and a new wheel is born at the left end. The full sweeps are the rare moments when the head reaches the right end of the tape.

sections.heading: Wheels that run out of road
html: A wheel drains the block on its right, and a block can run empty. Then the two gadgets on either side meet and something irregular happens: they merge into a short-lived gadget (100, 1, 10, …), or blocks merge, or a new wheel appears. These events are rare (a few dozen in 109 steps against tens of thousands of regular rounds) but they decide the shape of everything that follows.

State F, the only one that can halt, is used only in one such event: two g4 wheels meeting across an empty block. The five machines of the family differ exactly there: in this one the pair merges into a g2 and the next gadget advances (g2 → g3); from then on the tape is the same as for …_0RA1RF_0RC---, two steps earlier. F always reads a 0 there; a halt would need the pattern D>0 1 1, which no event seen so far produces.

sections.heading: A closed alphabet, but no closed set
html: One way to prove that a machine never halts is to find a set of tape shapes that contains the start, maps into itself, and never allows a halt. Here the shapes would be rows of gadgets with blocks of any length. The gadgets do close: the irregular events only ever produce eight more of them (1, 10, 100, 1001101, 10011010, 10011011, 100110110, 1001101100), so the alphabet is finite.

The set itself does not close. When the transient gadget 10 meets the transient gadget 1 across an empty block, the stretch 101 appears, and with the head arriving on it in D the machine halts (trap_halts, proved in Lean). Worse, b6 g4 b5 g3 b2 s b2 g0, a tape of regular gadgets with no empty block, also leads to a halt (witness_halts). Which tapes are safe depends on the block lengths, on whether two blocks empty at the same moment. That is arithmetic the shapes do not see.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.505). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 81,407 cells (62,637 left of the start, 52 right), with a density of 1s of 0.252.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE1LF_1LA0LB_1LD---: rename A→E, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→D, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state B, in a mirror
  • 1RB0LC_0RC1RF_1RD0RE_1LE0RA_0LA0LE_1RB---: rename A→C, B→D, C→E, D→A, E→B, F→F; it is this table started in state D

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB0RC_1LC0RD_0LD0LC_1RE0LA_0RA1RF_0RC---: 9,999,999 configurations, the last at step 9,999,998 here and step 10,000,000 there

family: nested base-5 odometer on blocks (1RB0RC_1LC0RD_0LD0LC_1RE0LA family)
summary: A nested base-5 odometer: gadgets between blocks of 1000s count mod 5 and carry right, a carry into the tape end inserts a new level; state F is reached only when two g4 gadgets collide across an empty block, and always reads 0 there.
